fact: The CIVICUS Monitor reports journalist Sandra Muhoza, convicted in December 2024 to 21 months for comments in a journalists' WhatsApp group, remained in prison in October 2025 although the Bujumbura Mairie Court of Appeal ruled on 30 May 2025 that the trial court lacked jurisdiction.
RSF says journalist Sandra Muhoza has been arbitrarily detained since April 2024 for relaying information about an alleged arms distribution in a private WhatsApp group.
SOS Medias Burundi reports the National Communication Council announced on 27 March 2025 the temporary suspension of the Yaga Burundi online media coalition, citing it was not registered.

Eu SEE (Hivos) reports that on 14 September 2026 Burundi's National Communications Council suspended a Yaga Burundi programme for six months after it aired a YouTube interview with Bonaventure Niyoyankana, a politician highly critical of the authorities.

SOS Medias Burundi reports that on 13 April 2026 the Ngozi Court of Appeal convicted journalist Sandra Muhoza of 'racial aversion' with six months already served, over information she relayed in a journalists' WhatsApp group about alleged arms distribution to ruling-party youths.
SOS Medias Burundi reports that in January 2026 Sandra Muhoza was sentenced to four years in a second proceeding over the same WhatsApp post, after more than 600 days in detention.

The Hivos-led Eu SEE snapshot says journalist Sandra Muhoza received a four-year prison sentence on 14 January 2026 after arrest for 'undermining national territorial integrity' and 'inciting racial hatred' over information shared in a private press group, and was paroled on 4 March 2026.

Human Rights Watch states that at the time of writing journalist Sandra Muhoza remained arbitrarily detained in Mpimba prison after conflicting judicial decisions, following the 13 June 2025 Mukaza Court of Appeal finding that it lacked jurisdiction.
